feedback.overall:
1. Overall assessment  
Strong senior digital communications CV with clear domain positioning, credible progression, and relevant public-sector impact. It reads professionally and is largely error-free, but it is somewhat dense and repetitive, with a few style/grammar inconsistencies that reduce sharpness.

1. Top strengths  
- Clear leadership narrative: strong progression at NACo from coordinator to director, reinforcing credibility and scope.  
- Good impact signals: 10,000+ page migration, 3.5M annual page views, 50+ publishers, and named tools/platforms add substance.  
- Well-aligned branding: headline, summary, competencies, and project examples consistently support a digital platform/communications leadership profile.

1. Top improvements  
- Reduce repetition and tighten structure: “digital strategy / governance / workflows / content operations” appears across summary, competencies, skills, and roles. Consolidate overlapping sections, especially “Core Competencies,” “Topline Skills,” and “Technical + IT.”  
- Add more outcome-focused metrics: several bullets describe responsibilities rather than results. Quantify gains in engagement, efficiency, adoption, campaign performance, or cost savings where possible.  
- Fix minor style inconsistencies: “social, and multimedia” has an unnecessary comma; “organization-wide” vs. “organization’s” usage varies; “A2/Learning” is awkward—use “French (A2, learning)”; title case is inconsistent across sections. No major misspellings or typos found.
feedback.intro:
Quick assessment: Strong positioning and clear seniority, but the intro is broad and overlaps heavily with the subtitle, core competencies, and work experience. It would be stronger with sharper outcomes, clearer scope, and slightly less list-like phrasing.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Tighten and differentiate from the subtitle by emphasizing public-sector scale and leadership impact, not just capability areas.
- Replace “building the platforms, governance models and content operations behind” with more direct wording like “leading” or “modernizing.”
- Consider a rewrite such as: “Senior digital leader with 12+ years of experience leading web modernization, digital governance, analytics, and content operations for high-volume public-sector organizations. Builds scalable editorial and platform systems that improve publishing, discovery, and audience engagement across web, email, multimedia, and AI-enabled experiences.”
- Use parallel style and consistent punctuation: add the serial comma in “platforms, governance models, and content operations.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “AI-enabled user experiences” overlaps with core competencies and recent projects; keep it brief here.
- “Enterprise web modernization, analytics infrastructure, editorial systems, multimedia production” repeats multiple skills sections almost verbatim.
feedback.coreCompetencies:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant themes, but this block overlaps heavily with the header and Topline Skills. It would be more effective if tightened into broader, less repetitive categories with parallel phrasing.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Use shorter, category-style phrases and keep structure parallel; e.g. noun phrases rather than mixed concepts.
- Reduce overlap with the header by emphasizing capability areas, not repeating “AI-enabled,” “analytics infrastructure,” and “multimedia production” verbatim.
- Consider this rewrite: Enterprise web modernization • Digital governance and editorial operations • Analytics, reporting and optimization • Multi-channel communications leadership • Search, discovery and content experience design • Workflow automation and platform integration • Public-sector advocacy communications • Video, livestream and multimedia production
- Replace “operations” repetition where possible to improve rhythm and readability.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Enterprise website modernization,” “analytics and reporting infrastructure,” and “AI-enabled…experiences” repeat language already used in the header.
- This section also overlaps with Topline Skills; keep Core Competencies high-level and let Topline/Technical sections carry the detail.
feedback.footer:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant project snapshot, but it reads dense and repeats themes already covered in Work Experience. Tightening phrasing and foregrounding outcomes or scope will make it more distinctive and scannable.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Add dates or “Selected Recent Projects” to reinforce recency and separate this from role bullets.
- Use parallel, tighter phrasing: “Built/Developed/Launched…” and trim stacked nouns like “structured content workflows.”
- Add one concrete signal of scale, audience, or purpose where possible (for example, legislative content, campaign growth, conference activation, recurring series cadence).
- Standardize style: spell out “10-by-20-foot” instead of “10×20-foot,” and consider “AI-powered” or “AI-enabled” consistently across the CV.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- AI Hybrid Search, microsite work, and advocacy video series substantially overlap with the current freelance and NACo experience bullets.
- The anniversary campaign is the most distinct item; consider emphasizing it first or keeping only the most differentiated projects here.

Leads enterprise web modernization, analytics infrastructure, editorial systems, multimedia production and AI-enabled user experiences for complex, mission-driven organizations.

items.title: Website

items.title: Core Competencies
items.content: Enterprise website modernization • Digital governance & editorial systems • Analytics and reporting infrastructure • Multi-channel communications operations • AI-enabled search and content experiences • Workflow automation and platform integration • Advocacy and public-sector communications • Multimedia production and livestream operations

items.title: CV Footer
items.content:
### Recent Projects
**AI Hybrid Search**
Designed an AI-enabled legislative search experience combining hybrid retrieval, structured content workflows, vector search and bill-level AI chat to improve discovery of complex policy content.
**We Are Counties Microsite**
Built a Drupal 10 campaign microsite with custom navigation, interactive storytelling modules, downloadable resources and a modular structure designed for continued campaign growth.
**Organization Anniversary Campaign**
Developed a multi-part digital campaign combining editorial storytelling, archival media, web features and a 10×20-foot interactive conference display connected to the main site.
**Advocacy Video Series**
Built a recurring advocacy video program spanning editorial planning, production and distribution across website, email and social channels.

items.title: Strategic Communications Consultant
items.subtitle: Freelance (full-time engagement)
items.content:
Support a U.S.-based national membership organization on digital strategy, campaign platforms, content operations and enterprise web improvement.
- Build and refine digital systems, workflows and analytics that support coordinated organization-wide communications.
- Develop campaign and storytelling experiences within the organization’s Drupal platform, including custom microsite structures, modular content sections and downloadable member-facing toolkits.
- Deliver CMS development, front-end implementation and technical troubleshooting for large public-facing web properties.
- Advise on governance, usability and operational best practices across web, email, social and multimedia channels.
- Lead development of an AI-enabled search initiative, shaping retrieval strategy, structured content workflows and user-facing discovery design.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, current role with good scope, but it reads as a task list and overlaps heavily with the header, skills, and project footer. Tighten it around 3–5 high-impact contributions and add outcomes, scale, or named initiatives.

Suggested edit:
- Open with a sharper lead: “Embedded consultant for a U.S. national membership organization, leading digital platform strategy, Drupal campaign delivery, and communications operations modernization.”
- Replace generic verbs (“support,” “advise”) with ownership verbs: led, built, launched, redesigned, standardized, improved.
- Consolidate overlapping bullets into outcome-led points, e.g.:
- Built Drupal campaign and storytelling experiences, including modular microsites, reusable content components, and downloadable member toolkits.
- Improved communications operations by redesigning workflows, analytics, and governance across web, email, social, and multimedia.
- Led an AI-enabled search initiative spanning retrieval design, structured content workflows, and user discovery experience.
- Add metrics where possible: number of sites/pages/users, publishing teams supported, time saved, engagement lift, search success, or reduced troubleshooting volume.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “AI-enabled search” and the microsite work already appear in Recent Projects; keep this entry higher-level unless you remove those project blurbs.
- Governance/analytics/workflow language overlaps with the NACo Director role; emphasize what is new or more advanced here.

items.title: Director of Digital Media
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led NACo’s digital communications team, overseeing the organization’s website, email, social media and video platforms, along with digital strategy, analytics, governance and budget management.
- Led the redesign and migration of NACo’s 10,000+ page website into a new Drupal platform supporting 3.5 million annual page views, 6,000+ average daily users and 50+ internal publishers.
- Directed NACo’s core digital communications channels, including email newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and social media platforms serving thousands of followers.
- Built NACo’s first broadcast-quality in-house video studio, expanding in-house capacity for advocacy programming, event production and recurring multimedia content.
- Expanded the organization’s analytics infrastructure across GA4, Microsoft Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio and BigQuery, improving reporting and strategic decision-making.
- Strengthened digital operations through clearer governance, publishing standards and cross-department planning systems.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, high-impact leadership entry with solid scale metrics. It should be tightened to foreground outcomes and avoid repeating channel-management details covered in earlier NACo roles.

Suggested edit:
- Open with a sharper scope/outcome line: “Directed NACo’s digital media function, leading web, email, social, video, analytics, governance, and budget across enterprise communications.”
- Combine and tighten web modernization bullet: “Led redesign and migration of a 10,000+ page website to Drupal, supporting 3.5M annual page views, 6,000+ daily users, and 50+ internal publishers.”
- Make analytics/governance bullets more outcome-led: add reporting speed, decision-making, publishing consistency, or cross-team adoption if measurable.
- Strengthen video bullet with business value: “Built NACo’s first broadcast-quality in-house studio, increasing internal production capacity for advocacy, events, and recurring multimedia programming.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Directed core digital communications channels” overlaps with the Associate Communications Director entry; either cut it or add distinct scale/results.
- “Publishing standards/editorial coordination” also echoes earlier NACo roles; keep this version focused on enterprise governance and systems.

items.title: Associate Communications Director
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social media and video, helping scale NACo’s editorial coordination and advocacy communications.
- Managed four recurring weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.
- Produced and expanded a weekly advocacy video update, helping establish video as a recurring policy communications channel.
- Strengthened editorial planning and coordination across communications, advocacy and program teams.
- Helped improve the consistency and effectiveness of NACo’s digital publishing workflows.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression story, but this entry overlaps heavily with the later Director role and earlier Digital Media Manager role. Make it more clearly about executional leadership, channel growth, and cross-team coordination at the manager-to-director transition point.

Suggested edit:
- Open with a tighter scope/result line: “Managed NACo’s day-to-day digital communications across web, email, social and video, scaling editorial coordination and advocacy messaging for a national county-official audience.”
- Combine newsletter detail into one impact bullet: “Owned production of four weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.”
- Sharpen the video bullet: “Launched and grew a weekly advocacy video update, establishing video as a recurring policy communications channel.”
- Rephrase the last two bullets to show operational leadership: “Built stronger editorial planning across communications, advocacy and program teams, and improved digital publishing workflows for more consistent, timely delivery.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Established video as a recurring channel” overlaps with the footer project and 2015–2018 role; keep only the scale/growth angle here.
- Avoid repeating broad channel oversight already covered more strategically in the Director role.

items.title: Digital Strategy & Content Leadership
items.content:
- Enterprise digital strategy
- Editorial systems and governance
- Multi-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector and advocacy messaging
- Audience-focused content planning
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong themes, but this skills block is too generic and overlaps heavily with the header, core competencies, and recent experience. Tighten it to emphasize senior-level scope and distinctiveness rather than repeating broad communications language.

Suggested edit:
- Replace generic phrases with sharper, higher-signal wording tied to current positioning:
- Enterprise digital strategy & web modernization
- Editorial governance, publishing workflows & content operations
- Cross-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector, membership & advocacy communications
- Audience strategy, content planning & user-centered messaging
- Consider reducing to 4 bullets to improve scannability and avoid padding.
- Use parallel noun phrases throughout; avoid mixing “leadership,” “messaging,” and “planning” without a consistent structure.
- If space allows elsewhere, move “audience-focused” concepts into a results-oriented experience bullet rather than a topline skill.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Enterprise digital strategy” and “editorial systems and governance” duplicate both the header and Core Competencies almost verbatim.
- “Public-sector and advocacy messaging” overlaps with multiple NACo roles; “membership” would add useful specificity.

items.title: Web Platforms & Technical Execution
items.content:
- Drupal
- WordPress
- SharePoint
- Power Pages
- CMS modernization
- HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery
- API integrations
- Workflow automation
- Airtable systems
- AI-enabled search experiences
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant skill cluster, but it reads as a raw tool list and overlaps heavily with the “Technical + IT” section. For a topline skills area, make it more strategic, grouped, and tied to recent strengths.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite as grouped capabilities, not a long stack list: “Drupal, WordPress, SharePoint & Power Pages • CMS modernization & migration • Front-end implementation (HTML, CSS, JavaScript, jQuery) • API integrations & workflow automation • Airtable-based systems • AI-enabled search and content discovery”
- Put highest-value, most recent strengths first: lead with Drupal, CMS modernization, AI-enabled search, and integrations.
- Replace “Airtable systems” with “Airtable-based systems” or “Airtable workflow systems” for clearer business relevance.
- If space allows elsewhere, quantify in experience bullets instead of here (e.g., Drupal migration of 10,000+ pages; AI search initiative leadership).

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This item substantially duplicates the “Technical + IT” section; keep this version high-level and leave specific tools/platforms to Technical + IT.
- “Workflow automation” also overlaps with Core Competencies and Technical + IT.

items.title: Analytics, Insights & Optimization
items.content:
- GA4
- Microsoft Clarity
- Looker Studio
- Power BI
- BigQuery
- KPI design
- Leadership reporting
- SEO and performance analysis
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant skill cluster that aligns with the 2022–2024 director role, but it reads as a tool list rather than a value statement. Tightening it around insight generation and decision support will make it feel more senior and less repetitive.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from tools-first to outcomes-first, e.g. “Analytics strategy, KPI design, executive reporting, and digital performance optimization.”
- Group tools compactly: “GA4, BigQuery, Looker Studio, Power BI, and Microsoft Clarity” rather than listing each as separate bullets.
- Replace “Leadership reporting” with stronger phrasing like “Executive dashboards and decision-support reporting.”
- Consider revised line: “Analytics strategy and KPI design • Executive dashboards and decision-support reporting • GA4, BigQuery, Looker Studio, Power BI, Microsoft Clarity • SEO and digital performance analysis”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This overlaps with “Data analytics & reporting” in Core Competencies and the NACo bullet about expanding analytics infrastructure; keep this section tool-and-scope focused, not achievement-focused.
- Avoid repeating generic “optimization” language already implied by digital strategy and performance analysis.

items.title: Multimedia Production & Event Delivery
items.content:
- Video production and editing
- Livestreaming
- PTZ camera systems
- Studio operations
- Hybrid and virtual event production
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong supporting skill area, but it reads generic and overlaps with “Multimedia & live event production” in Core Competencies plus multiple NACo bullets. Make it more specific to current/recent capability and tools, not broad category labels.

Suggested edit:
- Replace with tighter, higher-signal phrasing: “Broadcast video production • Livestream and hybrid event delivery • PTZ camera operation • Studio buildout and operations • Virtual event technical production”
- If space allows, emphasize leadership/scale over task wording: “In-house studio operations” or “Broadcast-quality studio operations” ties directly to the recent Director role.
- Use parallel noun phrases; avoid mixing “production and editing” with standalone tools/processes.
- If you can substantiate it elsewhere, add one stronger qualifier such as “multi-camera” or “end-to-end” before video production.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This duplicates “Multimedia & live event production” in Core Competencies; consider keeping the category here but removing the broader phrase there.
- “Studio operations” may undersell the stronger achievement in work history: building NACo’s first broadcast-quality in-house studio.

items.title: University of Virginia
items.subtitle: Bachelor of Arts (BA), Economics & History
items.content: Ranked among the top public universities in the United States
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: The current line adds little value and reads like generic school marketing. For an experienced candidate, this education entry should be minimal and factual unless you have honors or distinctions worth adding.

Suggested edit:
- Replace the content line entirely with no body text; the degree, school, location, and dates are sufficient.
- If applicable, swap in a concrete credential instead: “Relevant coursework: …” or “Honors: …” only if genuinely strong and still relevant.
- Tighten the subtitle to “B.A., Economics and History” for cleaner formatting.
- Consider dropping dates if you want to reduce age signaling and keep focus on recent senior experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Ranked among the top public universities…” is generic and not candidate-specific, so it weakens the entry rather than strengthening it.
- Avoid adding coursework unless it clearly supports current digital strategy/communications work; otherwise it will feel disconnected from the stronger recent experience.

items.title: Web Platforms & CMS
items.content: Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid, relevant platform list, but it reads as a bare inventory and overlaps heavily with “Topline Skills.” Since Drupal is central to recent roles, this item should emphasize depth/relevance or be trimmed to avoid repetition.

Suggested edit:
- Reorder by strongest recent relevance: **Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages**
- If space allows, add light proficiency framing: **Drupal (enterprise content architecture, migrations) • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages**
- Consider renaming to sharpen scope: **CMS & Web Publishing Platforms**
- If you want more impact, replace GitHub Pages with a more business-relevant platform only if used materially in recent work.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This largely duplicates **Topline Skills > Web Platforms & Technical Execution**; consider keeping platforms in one place only.
- Drupal already appears prominently in recent experience, so avoid repeating it elsewhere without added context.

items.title: Coding & Technical Implementation
items.content: HTML5 • CSS3 • JavaScript • jQuery • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid technical stack, but this item reads as a generic keyword list and overlaps heavily with “Topline Skills.” Make it more current and implementation-focused, emphasizing tools you actively use in recent roles.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe around applied execution, not just languages: “Front-end implementation: HTML5, CSS3, JavaScript, jQuery”
- Group modern tooling separately: “Technical implementation & deployment: API integrations, Google Tag Manager, Cloudflare Workers, GitHub Actions”
- If accurate, add scope or use case tied to recent work: e.g., “for Drupal builds, campaign microsites, tagging, and workflow automation”
- Consider dropping version-specific labels (“HTML5,” “CSS3”) unless needed; “HTML, CSS, JavaScript” is cleaner

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Strong overlap with “Topline Skills > Web Platforms & Technical Execution,” which already lists HTML, CSS, JavaScript, jQuery, API integrations, and workflow automation
- If you keep both sections, use this item for tools/platforms only and leave broader capability language to “Topline Skills”

items.title: Automation & Workflow Systems
items.content: Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana • Basecamp • Slack • Teams • Trello
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is clear but reads as a generic tool dump. Since workflow architecture already appears strongly in the summary, core competencies, and recent roles, this section should be tighter and more intentionally framed around systems you actively build or manage.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: **Workflow Automation & Collaboration Tools**
- Reorder by strongest/most relevant tools first: **Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana • Trello • Slack • Microsoft Teams • Basecamp**
- If accurate, add light functional grouping for readability: **Automation:** Airtable, Power Automate, Zapier | **Project/work management:** Jira, Asana, Trello, Basecamp | **Team collaboration:** Slack, Microsoft Teams
- If one or two tools were central in recent roles, consider signaling depth: **Airtable (workflow systems), Power Automate (process automation), Jira/Asana (project operations)**

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Workflow automation” and “Airtable systems” already appear in Topline Skills; avoid repeating that exact phrasing here.
- Slack and Teams are common collaboration tools; keep them only if they support the workflow/systems positioning.

items.title: Email & Engagement Systems
items.content: Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is relevant, but it reads as a bare vendor list and undersells your email-platform leadership. Since recent roles emphasize email operations and systems, frame these as platforms you’ve administered or used to support large-scale engagement.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: **Email Marketing & Engagement Platforms**
- Rewrite as: **Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp (campaign operations, newsletter publishing, audience segmentation, and engagement workflows)**
- If accurate, strengthen further with scope: **Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp — used to manage newsletter distribution, audience segmentation, automated journeys, and member communications**
- Keep platform names only if space is tight; otherwise add 3–5 words of function to show applied expertise, not just familiarity.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Avoid repeating “email newsletters reaching tens of thousands” here; that impact is already stronger in the NACo experience bullets.
- Don’t add generic “digital communications” language—this section should stay tool-specific to complement, not duplicate, Core Competencies.

items.title: Data, Analytics & Optimization
items.content: GA4 • Microsoft Clarity • Looker Studio • Power BI • BigQuery • SEO • A/B testing • Dashboarding
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant tool stack, but this line is too generic and overlaps heavily with “Topline Skills.” In a technical section, make it tighter and more implementation-focused rather than repeating broad capability labels.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite as: **GA4 • BigQuery • Power BI • Looker Studio • Microsoft Clarity • Google Search Console • A/B testing • KPI/dashboard reporting**
- Replace **SEO** with a tool or clearer technical capability (e.g., **Google Search Console**, **technical SEO**, or **performance analysis**) to keep the list concrete.
- Replace **Dashboarding** with **KPI/dashboard reporting** or **executive reporting** for sharper phrasing.
- Order by strongest/recently evidenced tools first: GA4, BigQuery, Power BI, Looker Studio, Clarity.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- This item substantially duplicates **Topline Skills → Analytics, Insights & Optimization**; consider trimming one of the two or making this version tools-only.
- “A/B testing” is not evidenced elsewhere in recent experience; keep it only if you can support it in a role/project bullet.

items.title: Work Eligibility
items.content: Full legal authorization to work in Belgium (Visa D + residence permit / carte de séjour)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Useful for Belgium-based applications, but the phrasing is a bit legalistic and takes more space than needed. This should read as a clear status note, not a headline achievement.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite for brevity and recruiter scanability: “Authorized to work in Belgium (Visa D and residence permit).”
- If accurate, make it stronger and simpler: “Fully authorized to work in Belgium; residence permit in place.”
- Avoid the French term unless the role specifically requires bilingual administrative terminology; “residence permit” is usually enough.
- Consider moving this into the contact/header area for local applications, since eligibility matters more there than in a secondary rail.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- No major duplication, but this item is lower-value than recent experience; keep it very short so it doesn’t compete for attention.
- If location/contact already signals Belgium and applications are local, this may be optional rather than essential.

items.title: Languages
items.content:
**English** (Native)
**French** (A2/Learning)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is clear but too compressed and visually awkward. It should be reformatted for quick scanning and framed honestly so French supports your Belgium-based role without overstating proficiency.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite as a simple line: Languages: English (native) | French (A2, currently improving)
- Use lowercase proficiency style for consistency and cleaner tone: native, A2, conversational/basic if accurate.
- If relevant to target roles, add practical context only if true: French (A2, professional working improvement underway)
- Keep it concise; this section is supporting information, not a selling point versus your recent digital leadership experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- No major duplication, but avoid overdesign/bolding here; the CV already has strong skills sections competing for attention.
- If space is tight, this can stay in the rail and should not be repeated in the header, summary, or cover letter unless language is job-relevant.

items.title: Soft Skills
items.content: Cross-department coordination • Stakeholder communication • Team leadership • Strategic planning • Clear writing and editing • Problem-solving • Adaptability
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This section is too generic and largely repeats strengths already proven in the summary and core competencies. On a senior CV, “soft skills” should either be removed or reframed as leadership traits tied to scope and outcomes.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to “Leadership Strengths” or “Management & Collaboration” to sound more senior and less filler.
- Cut generic items like “Problem-solving” and “Adaptability”; keep only traits that support target roles.
- Tighten to 4–5 items max, e.g.: Cross-functional leadership • Executive stakeholder management • Editorial judgment • Team development • Strategic planning
- If space is tight, remove this section entirely and use the room for quantified achievements in recent roles.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-department coordination” and “Stakeholder communication” duplicate the header summary and Core Competencies.
- “Team leadership” and “Strategic planning” are already demonstrated more credibly in the 2022–2024 Director role.

items.title: References
items.content: References available upon request.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item adds little value and uses space that could better support recent, higher-impact experience. “References available upon request” is assumed by most employers and usually should be removed.

Suggested edit:
- Delete the “References” entry entirely.
- Use the freed space for stronger supporting content instead, such as a brief “Selected Results” rail item with 1–2 metrics from recent roles.
- If references are specifically requested, provide them separately rather than on the CV.
- If you want a replacement rail item, consider “Work Authorization” or “Languages,” which are more useful and already present here.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This section is redundant because reference availability is standard and does not differentiate you.
- Keeping it may weaken the second-page rail by displacing more relevant, recent qualifications.

items.title: Digital Media Manager / Producer
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Advanced through two digital roles, supporting the creation of the organization’s first in-house digital team and strengthening workflows across web, email, social, and multimedia. Contributed to a major website refresh and produced high-impact digital content—including livestreams and weekly video updates—while providing day-to-day guidance to a digital media associate.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression signal, but the item is too general and overlaps with later NACo roles. Make it more execution-focused and specific to early-team building, production, and platform support.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite to emphasize foundational contributions: “Promoted across two digital roles and helped establish NACo’s first in-house digital team, supporting web, email, social, and multimedia operations.”
- Add clearer ownership and outputs: “Supported a major website refresh, produced livestreams and recurring video content, and improved day-to-day publishing workflows across channels.”
- Tighten the management line: replace “providing day-to-day guidance” with “mentored a digital media associate” or “supervised a digital media associate’s daily production work.”
- If possible, add 1–2 metrics: number of livestreams/videos produced, publishing volume, audience growth, or workflow/time savings.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “weekly video updates” overlaps with the 2018–2022 role; keep this entry focused on launching/producing the format, not expanding it.
- “strengthening workflows” is repeated elsewhere; specify early-stage team/process building here instead.

items.title: County Solutions & Innovations Coordinator
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Coordinated innovation and research projects supporting organizational programs and policy work. Contributed to digital content production and multimedia materials, and launched the organization’s first podcast, overseeing planning, scripting, and production.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid early-career entry, but it reads broadly and overlaps with later NACo roles in digital/media. Emphasize the podcast launch as the clearest differentiator and tighten the research/program support language.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite to foreground the unique achievement: “Coordinated innovation and research initiatives supporting county-focused programs and policy work; launched NACo’s first podcast, leading concept development, scripting, guest coordination, and production.”
- Replace vague phrases like “contributed to digital content production” with a more active, specific clause such as “produced multimedia and digital content assets for program and policy communications.”
- If possible, add scope or outcome: number of episodes, audience, internal stakeholders supported, or how the podcast/content supported advocacy, member engagement, or organizational visibility.
- Keep this entry to 1 sentence or 2 short bullets so it doesn’t compete with stronger, more recent digital leadership roles.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Digital content production and multimedia materials” overlaps with later digital/media roles; keep this item focused on research coordination + first podcast launch.
- Avoid language about leading digital strategy or operations here, since that is better established in 2015–2024 roles.

items.title: Multimedia & Creative Tools
items.content: Premiere Pro • Audition • Photoshop • Illustrator • Livestream studio workflows • Podcast production
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid supporting skills list, but it reads a bit generic and overlaps with stronger multimedia claims already made elsewhere. Tighten it to emphasize tools/software and frame production capabilities in more specific, current terms.

Suggested edit:
- Replace broad phrases with clearer, tool-led wording: “Adobe Premiere Pro • Adobe Audition • Adobe Photoshop • Adobe Illustrator • Livestream production workflows • Podcast recording/editing”
